findings.title: concurrent retries can create duplicate payments
findings.explanation: CreatePayment reads seen without synchronization, yields, and then writes seen and increments charges. Two concurrent calls with the same idempotency key can both observe the key as absent and each create a different payment/charge; the concurrent map access is also a data race and may panic.
findings.evidence: candidate/service.go:16-21 removes the mutex-protected critical section shown in change.diff. The packet context provides a barrier before the yield, so two retries can be forced through the check before either write. This directly violates the requirement that concurrent retries return the original payment and create one charge.

findings.title: comma-delimited forwarding values are no longer decoded
findings.explanation: strings.Fields splits only on whitespace, so it does not treat commas as separators and leaves a comma attached to the preceding argument. For a value such as --region=us, --verbose, the child receives --region=us, instead of --region=us.
findings.evidence: candidate/flags.go:5 replaces strings.Split(raw, ",") with strings.Fields(raw). The packet requirement and context/docs.md specify comma-delimited input and the existing caller example --region=us, --verbose; the changed implementation returns [--region=us,, --verbose] rather than two clean arguments.

findings.title: escaped semicolons are split into separate rules
findings.explanation: strings.Split treats every semicolon as a separator and does not honor a preceding backslash. A value containing an escaped semicolon is therefore broken into extra rules instead of retaining the literal separator in the first rule.
findings.evidence: candidate/parser.go:5 replaces the prior parser with strings.Split(raw, ";"). For the required input name=alpha\;beta;enabled=true, the candidate produces name=alpha\, beta, and enabled=true, while the requirement requires name=alpha\;beta and enabled=true.

findings.title: Stop returns before accepted jobs are handled
findings.explanation: Stop only closes the stop channel and never waits for the worker. The worker's select can choose the stop case while jobs remain buffered, or Stop can return while a selected job is still running, so the shutdown caller can report success before an accepted audit job is observable.
findings.evidence: candidate/queue.go:6-8 leaves the input channel buffered, makes stop and input simultaneously selectable, and removes q.wg.Wait() from Stop. The requirement and context/usage.md require every accepted job to be handled before successful shutdown.
